subject: biology
note: IGCSE-only concepts (new notes) and the IGCSE spec points that join existing GCSE concepts. Merged with gcse-biology.json by conceptMap.ts. Each IGCSE spec point is primary in exactly one concept.

concepts.title: Characteristics and kingdoms of living organisms
concepts.scope: The characteristics of living things, dichotomous keys, and the features that place organisms in the animal, plant, fungus, prokaryote, protoctist and virus groups.

concepts.title: Balanced diet and nutrients
concepts.scope: What a balanced diet is, the sources and uses of each nutrient group, fibre, water, vitamins C and D, calcium and iron, and the deficiency diseases scurvy and rickets.

concepts.title: Teeth and physical digestion
concepts.scope: Types and structure of human teeth, their jobs in physical digestion, and the stomach churning food to increase surface area for enzymes.

concepts.title: Absorption in the small intestine
concepts.scope: How nutrients and water are absorbed in the small intestine and colon, and how villi and microvilli, capillaries and lacteals are adapted for absorption.

concepts.title: Water movement through the plant
concepts.scope: The route of water from root hair to leaf, tracing it with a stain, evaporation and loss through stomata, transpiration pull and cohesion, and why plants wilt.

concepts.title: Cholera and controlling the spread of disease
concepts.scope: How clean water, hygienic food, personal hygiene, waste disposal and sewage treatment control disease, with cholera as the case study including how its toxin causes diarrhoea.

concepts.title: Passive immunity
concepts.scope: Short-term immunity from antibodies passed from another person, across the placenta and in breast milk, why it gives no memory cells, and why breast-feeding matters.

concepts.title: Ventilation of the lungs and breathed air
concepts.scope: The parts of the breathing system, how ribs, intercostal muscles and diaphragm change thorax volume and pressure, cartilage in the trachea, and the composition of inspired and expired air.

concepts.title: Parts of the flower and pollination
concepts.scope: The parts of an insect-pollinated flower and their functions, the anthers and stigmas of a wind-pollinated flower, pollen grains, and pollination with adaptations of each type.

concepts.title: Fertilisation in flowering plants and germination
concepts.scope: Self- and cross-pollination and their effects on a population, pollen tube growth and fertilisation, and the conditions seeds need to germinate.

concepts.title: Human reproductive systems
concepts.scope: The parts of the male and female reproductive systems and their functions, and a comparison of male and female gametes.

concepts.title: Fertilisation, the embryo and the placenta
concepts.scope: Fertilisation of the egg, implantation of the embryo, and how the placenta, umbilical cord and amniotic sac support the fetus, including what can cross the placenta.

concepts.title: Food webs and feeding roles
concepts.scope: Food webs as networks of food chains, the terms herbivore, carnivore and decomposer, and using webs to predict the effect of overharvesting and introduced species.

concepts.title: Energy flow and pyramids of energy
concepts.scope: The Sun as the energy source, the flow of energy through organisms to the environment, and why pyramids of biomass and energy are better than pyramids of numbers.

concepts.title: Population growth
concepts.scope: Factors affecting population growth and the lag, exponential, stationary and death phases of the sigmoid growth curve, with the limiting factors behind each.

concepts.title: Enzymes in food and household products
concepts.scope: How pectinase, lactase and biological washing powders use enzymes, and how to investigate them.

concepts.title: Yeast and bacteria in food production
concepts.scope: How yeast makes bread rise by anaerobic respiration, how Lactobacillus turns milk into yoghurt, and how to investigate yeast in different conditions.
